newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Somalis end peace conference in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Somalis end peace conference in Ethiopia.

text.p: A peace conference bringing together many of Somalia's feuding factions ended on Thursday with an appeal for dialogue from Ethiopian Foreign Minister Seyoum Mesfin.
Seyoum told participants including powerful north Mogadishu faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed to pursue dialogue as the best way of rebuilding the broken Horn of Africa country.

The minister advised the wrangling Somalis from some 25 factions at the meeting in the Ethiopian capital Addis Ababa to heal their wounds before a major reconciliation conference in the Somali town of Bossasso in November.
Hussein Aideed, the faction leader in south Mogadishu and self-proclaimed president of Somalia, boycotted the Addis Ababa meeting.

"We call on you, not only to do your share in bridging the gap between you and others, most particularly between you and Hussein Aideed, but to do more to ensure that the national reconciliation conference in Bossasso is boycotted by no one," Seyoum said.
Somalia has been without central authority since 1991 when rebels overthrew dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, who is now dead. But they soon battled over control of the country and laid waste to it.
